messages:
incidents-bot: INCIDENT 3067894321 — Streaming decode p99 > SLO (us-west-2, streaming-api). Current p99: 1.8s (SLO 1.0s). Affected routes: /v1/chat/stream, /v1/decode. Paging signals: kernel compilepath evictions ticking up.

Maya (sre-oncall): ack. pinging runtime + infra. any deploys/changes overnight?

Ravi (runtime-eng): we pushed TRT8 + FlashAttention optimized kernels to canary pools @ 02:12 UTC, rolled to majority at 03:05 UTC with new compile flag -DENABLE_FLASHATTN=1.

Maya (sre-oncall): timeline ok — metrics show jump around 03:10. can you confirm whether the new kernels have fallback to legacy kernels?

Ravi (runtime-eng): they should, but fallback path isn't exercised for streaming due to our kernel selection heuristic. suspect FlashAttn path for long sequences is causing increased per-request memory churn -> more host<->device paging.

metrics-bot: (5m) decode_streaming_p99{region="us-west-2"} = 1.83s, decode_streaming_p95 = 0.62s, decode_streaming_error_rate = 0.9%. paging_evictions_rate = +420% vs baseline.

Sofia (infra): seeing elevated minor page faults on nodes with new kernel build. dmesg shows repeated cgroup/memory pressure OOM warn on gpu driver side.

Maya (sre-oncall): can we get quick diagnostics: nodemetrics, top, and nvidia-smi from affected hosts? runbook step 2 -> paste kubectl and dmesg snippets here.

Ravi (runtime-eng): grabbing from pod decoder-ff3b (node ip 10.12.5.42):

```
$ kubectl -n inference exec decoder-ff3b -- sh -c "cat /proc/meminfo | egrep 'MemAvailable|SwapFree'"
MemAvailable:       824412 kB
SwapFree:         2097152 kB
```

```
$ kubectl -n inference exec decoder-ff3b -- sh -c "dmesg | tail -n 30"
[ 12345.678901] nvhost: memcg: gpu memory cgroup eviction requested
[ 12345.679012] nvhost: memcg: paging to host triggered for client decode_v2
[ 12345.679125] nvhost: WARNING: flash_attn kernel - high page-faults
```

```
$ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,utilization.gpu,fb_memory.used --format=csv -i 0
2026/03/15 03:14:12, 98 %, 14237 MiB
```
```
$ ps aux | grep decoder
root       2321 95.4 12.3 2345678 123456 ?   Ssl 03:13  12:34 /usr/local/bin/decoder --kernel=flashattn
```

Maya (sre-oncall): confirms memcg evictions; that aligns with paging signals. we need an immediate mitigation to stop SLO breach for customers. proposed mitigations: 1) route streaming traffic to stable pool (no flashattn), 2) temporarily disable FlashAttention kernel via env var, 3) enable prefix/KV cache to reduce decode work, 4) raise error budget alerts to comms.

Ravi (runtime-eng): preparing a canary rollback patch: set RUNTIME_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=legacy on the streaming deployment and patch node taints so routing moves to legacy pool. patch command ready:

```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/decoder RUNTIME_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=legacy
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/decoder
```

Sofia (infra): I'll cordon nodes running new kernel to prevent new pods landing and mark existing as unschedulable for canary autoscaler:

```
kubectl cordon ip-10-12-5-42
kubectl label node ip-10-12-5-42 kernel=quarantine
```

Maya (sre-oncall): execute route + restart. I'll open a customer impact note and notify support. Ethan, if you come online please take 2nd.

Ethan (sre-2nd): on it — applying env override now.

Ethan (sre-2nd): applied override, restarting pods (03:23). watch metrics for p99 drop.

metrics-bot: 03:27: decode_streaming_p99 us-west-2 = 0.98s. errors down to 0.2%. paging_evictions_rate trending down.

customer-ops: ping — any ETA on full rollback vs hotpatch? customers asking about 5-10% request retries.

Maya (sre-oncall): short term -> keep legacy override until patch validated. longer term -> need fix in kernel compilepath to avoid host paging: options discussed: build with smaller workspace, adjust allocator, or fall back to float16 kernel where memory pressure is lower. add RFC for kernel selection heuristic to prefer fallback under memcg pressure.

Ravi (runtime-eng): agree. will open PR with two changes: (1) patch FlashAttn kernel to reduce temporary allocations (2) add runtime guard that checks memcg page-fault rate and switches to legacy kernel automatically. PR link: https://git.redwood/runtime/pulls/4321 (work in progress).

Maya (sre-oncall): incident summary for handoff ->
- impact: p99 streaming decode spiked to ~1.8s, p95 mostly within SLO but tail affected, error spike ~0.9%
- cause hypothesis: new TRT8/FlashAttention kernel path increases transient GPU host paging under certain long-sequence streaming workloads; memcg evictions observed
- mitigation: set RUNTIME_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=legacy for streaming deploys; cordon/quarantine canary nodes; restart decoder pods -> p99 recovered to ~1.0s
- next steps: runtime team to PR patch for allocator + runtime memcg guard; infra to evaluate node-level swap/oom kconfig and driver updates; schedule postmortem if customer impact > 1% or >30m window

Ethan (sre-2nd): taking shift. I've saved commands and linked metrics graphs in incident tracker. please ping me if PR needs testing in canary.

Maya (sre-oncall): tagging followups -> @Ravi create PR, @Sofia check node driver version matrix vs TRT8, @customer-ops prepare customer-facing status note if we see re-regression.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT 3067894321 status -> mitigated. severity -> S2 (partial customer impact). duration -> 00:30:00.

Maya (sre-oncall): handing off to Ethan for next hour. leaving detailed notes in the thread. :white_check_mark:

Ethan (sre-2nd): acknowledged. will monitor p99 and memcg eviction metrics.

customer-ops: thanks all — I'll draft a short update to affected customers: summary + "we rolled back an optimized kernel that caused transient paging; stable path restored; engineering is implementing a fix". will post after review.

Ravi (runtime-eng): logging TODOs in the PR and adding unit+integration test to simulate memcg evictions. also toggling canary to run with new guard once tests pass.

Maya (sre-oncall): closing slack loop for now. keep this thread updated if we see new spikes.

metrics-bot: Final check 03:45: decode_streaming_p99 = 0.95s, paging_evictions_rate = baseline.
